finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm but ignores the boolean it returns, so the admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can run purgeAll().
finding.source: Any authenticated low-privilege user sends a request to the purge endpoint. The user comes from the request context.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the caller's User from the request context.
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for non-admins, but the result is discarded and there is no early return.

finding.guards_checked: rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 uses mustPerm correctly and returns on failure, so it is not affected. No middleware or other authorization wrapper exists in the codebase, which is a single file. checkPerm only returns a value and has no side effects such as writing a 403.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm (handlers.go:12) returns a bool with no side effects; its result is discarded at handlers.go:26. No middleware exists in the single-file codebase. mustPerm (handlers.go:16) is the enforcing variant and is used only in rotateKeys.
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm as a bare statement, so its false result for non-admins is discarded, and purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none effective: checkPerm (handlers.go:12) returns a bool and is called as a bare statement at line 26; mustPerm is only used in rotateKeys. No middleware exists in the directory.
verdict_facts.reason: handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's bool (defined at handlers.go:12-14, no side effects or 403) and handlers.go:27 calls purgeAll() unconditionally, so any authenticated user can trigger it.
